cells.tense: You are here with the pen, reading what's needed before it's spoken.
cells.ask: Pick one place your strength is going where it isn't needed and stop sending it there. Not withdrawal, just accuracy. Then look at what frees up for you and for them.
cells.core:
You can feel what a situation is asking for before anyone names it, and you can put some of what you have behind it. Not for credit and not waiting to be asked. You read the shape of a room and the strength moves with it, which is why the help lands.

One place to watch is a read that hasn't landed yet. This holds without forcing when what you give is exact, not when it's constant. So bring one thing tonight that is precisely what the moment requires and nothing more. Then let the result say whether the read was right — not you.
cells.sheetLine: You read what's needed and can put strength behind it.
cells.verb: share strength outward where it's needed
cells.place: a place where you see the pattern under the surface, stripped of content

cells.tense: You are ahead of the moment, bracing for a need that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Before you take on the next thing whose need hasn't been asked, put a name to what fairness requires here — one sentence about who should carry it. Then let that sentence decide what you lift.
cells.core:
You're already moving toward the need. The trouble is you've gone there before it arrived — supplying, holding, covering, being the one who can, and calling it support because stopping looks like standing by. What you're carrying is a picture of what might be needed, not the need itself.

Fairness is the measure that holds here. Without it, support starts to crush the person who asked and the one who didn't. Going ahead of what was wanted isn't generosity with force behind it. The way back is holding without forcing, and that starts by standing still long enough to find out what's actually required.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying needs that haven't reached you yet.
cells.verb: share strength outward where it's needed

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Pick a commitment you can end this month — a group, a standing obligation, a role only you keep afloat. Say out loud that it's finished. Leave once, without an inventory of what would happen without you.
cells.core:
Strength moving well goes out of you and comes back, you carry something for someone and then set it down, and receiving doesn't feel like a debt. You can map that flow from far enough away — plain pattern, stripped of the mess of being inside it — and you describe it well. What isn't running is the handoff: nothing leaves you, so nothing comes back.

You want to trust the exchange, but trust doesn't turn on. Finishing something and letting the release count as done, not defeat, turns it on. That puts you under the pattern instead of watching it. One ending, done cleanly, is enough to start the line moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You can see how support moves, so you don't have to enter it.

cells.tense: You are already holding the load while the pen sits on the table.
cells.ask: Name one thing you keep going for someone — one act, one person. Say it's yours, out loud or in a written line. Don't explain it. Let the claim stand for a day.
cells.core:
Going well, this looks like knowing which person you're holding, why this one, and saying so without ceremony. You are already the one who is there when a person can't be — a standing shape you recognize at once and trust. What isn't claimed is that you are the one doing it. You read the pattern right and call it the situation being what it is. That's your choice sitting unclaimed on the table.

What changes is naming one of them: which person, which act, why this one. Point at the support you're already giving and call it your call — not more giving, the recognition. The reading is already done. Claiming it is the part left.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one holding it. Stop calling it the situation.
